notes.detailedSummary: For smooth integral projective X over any algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and an actual big rational L, the reconstruction first produces nearby minimal references from a single model-obstacle multiplier-ideal net, without general closure. It then proves uniform bounds for all late incoming FS stages, usc comparison at old poles, positive guards, actual ample differences, downward directedness, and the all-point endpoint. The resulting envelope and compactness deductions are conditional on ordinary relative multiplier-ideal subadditivity/generation; actual-ample divisorial nonnegligibility is independently reconstructed from complete primary proof units and G0. DEL's retrieved generation proof has a complex absolute domain, so it does not finish the relative arbitrary-field input.
notes.text:
Retain k algebraically closed, trivially valued, characteristic zero; X smooth integral projective of arbitrary dimension n≥1; L an actual big rational bundle; A an actual ample rational bundle. Genuine PSH(c1(L)) means an all-point decreasing FS net on varying actual rational bundles whose numerical classes converge to c1(L), with finite generic limit. No countability, finite generation, toric, skeleton, or support restriction enters.

The independent reference construction uses a resolved actual test configuration for a model obstacle f in an actual big bundle B. Its relative complete-system base ideals a_m give increasing actual FS functions f+m^(-1)φ(a_m) with supremum Q_B(f), by normality and the all-point section-extension criterion. Assuming the ordinary relative multiplier-ideal inputs a_m⊂b_m, b_(mℓ)⊂b_m^ℓ, and one equivariant ample C making (mB+C)b_m globally generated, the actual functions Ψ_m=f+m^(-1)φ(b_m)+m^(-1)φ_C are FS in B+C/m. After φ_C≥0 they decrease in divisibility order, lie between Q_B(f) and f+φ_C/m, and have finite generic limit. Their limit is genuine by this ONE defining net. Competitors τ≤f are compared with Q_B(f) on divisorial points using an actual B=C0+E, C0 ample, E effective, and the section system (τ_j+ε_j log|s_E|)/(1+ε_j) in the actual B. Common ample G0 determination then gives P_B(f)=lim Ψ_m everywhere. Thus V_B=P_B(0) is available before general closure.

Here is the decisive proved pole lemma. If ψ≤0 is extended-continuous, F≥(1−δ)ψ−k, 0<δ<1, and h≤ψ+C, define D=h−F where F is finite and assign D=−∞ at F's poles. Off those poles D≤δψ+C+k. At a pole of F the floor forces ψ=−∞, and extended continuity sends that upper bound to −∞. Therefore D is usc there; no subtraction of two infinities is used. For decreasing h_i with strictly negative limiting comparison, the nested closed sets {D_i≥0} have empty intersection, so compactness gives an entire negative tail.

For a decreasing genuine u_i with finite-generic endpoint u, choose T_η=L+ηA and nearby B=L+εA, 0<ε<η/4. Take a normalized reference stage ψ on an actual R sufficiently late that T_η−R is ample. Choose δ>0 small so the ACTUAL bundle T_η−(1−δ)R is ample. Special stages are actual FS functions F in T_η with F≥u+κ for κ>0 and F≥(1−δ)ψ−k. Tensor both systems into the same specified T_η before taking their maximum. Every u_i, and every sufficiently late defining FS stage h of a fixed u_i, embeds into B; their generic values are uniformly bounded by M+1. Hence h≤V_B+M+1≤ψ+c_ψ+M+1, including old poles. This proves the previously missing uniform barrier hypothesis.

Given finitely many old F_l, choose a new η arbitrarily small and a new normalized reference stage ψ whose actual bundle R lies below every old B_l by an ample difference. Then ψ≤V_(B_l)≤ψ_l+c_l. Choose δ<min δ_l and k large; the new floor b=(1−δ)ψ−k obeys b−F_l≤(δ_l−δ)ψ_l+(1−δ)c_l+k_l−k off old poles and equals −∞ at them. Choose κ<min κ_l/4. Apply the pole lemma first to u_i+2κ, then to the defining FS tail of that one u_i. Obtain h+κ≤F_l for every l and an actual ample difference allowing tensoring into T_η. The new F=max(h+κ,b) is below every old stage and still above u+κ. Ordering these data by scalar decrease and η decrease gives one directed FS net. At each x and every real t>u(x), choose u_i(x), then a late h(x), then κ small and k large to obtain F(x)<t. This also treats u(x)=−∞. Thus the endpoint is u at every original point and classes tend to c1(L).

Model-majorant envelopes then give usc-obstacle envelopes, and usc suprema remain genuine. Compactness follows by embedding in one actual ample cone, taking regularized tail suprema, and using divisorial nonnegligibility. That last input was reconstructed through BJv4 Lemmas 2.28–2.29, the complete Lemma 4.26 proof at rendered L3624–3631, and Lemma 5.7/Theorem 5.6 at L4000–4022; only its ample regularization step uses G0. General big compactness and the rejected abstract Lemma 4.6 are not premises.

Limitation: retrieved DEL Theorem 1.8 supplies absolute generation on smooth complex projective varieties, not the required relative arbitrary-field result. The paper explains relative vanishing plus Castelnuovo–Mumford generation but retains their exact multiplier-ideal application as an external uncompleted proof obligation. Consequently this is a conditional foundation, not an unconditional P16.5 solution. notes.summary: Conditional target-independent entire energy and outer-operator reconstruction, with raw mass vol(L), actual original functions, and both continuous derivative signs. Finite central-model targets attain solutions; arbitrary-target existence and all-solution uniqueness remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Assuming n1's genuine foundations and the explicitly scoped ordinary algebraic volume/positive-product inputs, section lattices define a model obstacle energy and positive atomic derivatives retaining all central multiplicities. Actual continuous-majorant infima define the entire genuine relative E1 space. Truncated-volume coefficient estimates yield an operator on that space before any target choice, with every original continuous outer derivative and decreasing/energy continuity. A finite-dimensional argument solves targets supported on vertices of one actual snc model. Neither this conditional construction nor its finite-target endpoint proves the entire original equation theorem.
notes.text:
Use the retained domain and genuine foundation of n1. Put V=vol_X(L)>0. On a smooth equivariant modification Y of X×P1, with F=Σb_iE_i and vertical D, let α_D(c)=pullback(L)+D+cF. The relative complete-section module in degree m is a graded k[t] lattice in H0(X,mL)⊗k[t,t^−1]. An adapted basis has integer weights w_(m,j). Gluing to the product lattice at infinity gives the exact count h0(Y,mα_D(c))=Σ_j max(w_(m,j)+mc+1,0). For c sufficiently large all summands are positive, and full-section asymptotics give vol_Y(α_D(c))=(n+1)cV+(n+1)ℰ(D). The intercept is independent of c and higher model. Volume-root concavity gives concavity of ℰ; effective-divisor order and constant shifts give monotonicity and V-Lipschitz control.

The ordinary big-volume differential gives q_i=<α_D(c)^n>·E_i≥0. Applying the intercept identity uniformly near D in each E_i direction proves each coefficient is independent of large c; Σb_iq_i=V. Hence μ_D=Σb_iq_iδ_(x_i) is a positive original-carrier measure of raw mass V, not L^n. Effective exceptional divisors have zero coefficient because adding them to a pullback preserves sections on a normal base. This proves higher-model invariance. Differentiation gives dℰ(D+tH)/dt at zero =∫f_H dμ_D. No target enters.

For continuous f the actual section weight W_m(f;s)=inf_x[mf(x)−log|s|(x)] uses +∞ at section poles. Its superlevels form finite-dimensional flags. The floored normalized sums n!m^(−n−1)Σfloor W converge by model density and uniform flag comparison. A section term is genuine, so W_m(f;s)≥λ iff log|s|/m+λ/m≤P_θ(f), giving exact envelope-fiber descent. Define E_θ(u)=inf_(continuous f≥u)ℰ(f) on ACTUAL genuine functions and E1={E_θ>−∞}. The reference is V_θ=P_θ(0), E_θ(V_θ)=0; E shifts by cV. Compact comparison against finite continuous majorants proves energy continuity for arbitrary decreasing genuine nets. The actual floors max(u,V_θ−k) give the same finite-energy definition without subtracting poles. Model supporting planes are finite divisorial coordinate sums, and E is their infimum, proving weak upper semicontinuity and compact normalized cost sublevels.

For the entire outer construction, a nonpositive model obstacle of cost at most B has truncated volume g_D(c)=vol(α_D(c))/(n+1)=lim n!m^(−n−1)Σ(w+mc)_+. Its derivative mass is between V−B/c and V. The deficit ℰ(D)+cV−g_D(c) is the limit of sums min(w+mc,0), monotone under adding each effective central prime. Differentiating proves coefficientwise 0≤μ_(D,c)≤μ_D, with total variation loss at most B/c. This coefficient argument is needed because central primes need not be nef.

For fixed original model direction h and fixed large c, volume lower bounds and an upper fixed big class yield a uniform big neighborhood of every α_D(c). Homogeneity/order of positive products, paired separately with fixed nef representatives of the direction, gives a Taylor estimate |ℰ(D+th)−ℰ(D)−t∫h dμ_D|≤K_c t²/2+|t| ||h||(B+B')/c, where B'=B+2V||h||. First fix c, then let either sign of t tend to zero, then let c→∞. Apply this to cofinal model majorants of any normalized u∈E1. Their envelopes decrease all-point, their energies converge, and their measures have mass V. Every weak cluster has the same model-test integrals, identified with the two-sided derivative of E_θ(P_θ(u+th)); density makes the cluster unique. This constructs M_θ(u) independently of targets, with M_θ(u)(K)=V and derivative ∫h dM_θ(u) for every original continuous h. Ordered vanishing energy gaps also give decreasing weak-measure continuity. These deductions retain n1's conditional algebraic premise and ordinary algebraic positive-product inputs.

There is actual conditional finite-model attainment: on one snc model, genuine u≤f_D iff its finite vertex values meet the obstacle coordinates. The all-point direction follows from the Gauss center relation Σ b_iw(z_i)=1 and the regular-section weighted inequality. For desired positive masses p_i of sum V on a subset of vertices, give extra vertices sufficiently large inactive coordinates. The objective G(a)=E(P_θ(f_a))−Σp_i a_i is constant-invariant and, on max a_i=0, satisfies G≤VT−p_min osc(a). It attains a maximum. Holding extra coordinates fixed locally permits genuine coordinate differentiation; vanishing partial derivatives give precisely the prescribed atomic masses. Contact orthogonality gives zero masses at extra vertices. The resulting envelope is an actual E1 function on X^an and also maximizes the entire-cone objective for that finite target. This does not prove arbitrary-support existence or uniqueness among all genuine solutions.

notes.summary: Three confined mathematical checks: the abstract twice-closure counterexample remains valid; an actual ample P1 fixed-section limit has energy −∞; and a big nonnef blowup class has volume 4 although L²=3.
notes.detailedSummary: The old abstract pole obstruction is reproved without treating it as an actual FS counterexample. The P1 example independently uses the granted ample curve model formula, so it is not conditional on the big-class reconstruction: f_k=max(log|z1|,−k) has MA δ_(k ord_p), energy −k/2, and decreasing one-section limit of infinite negative energy. On Bl_p(P2), L=2H+E has section count binomial(2m+2,2), hence volume 4 rather than self-intersection 3. Exact finite arithmetic illustrates these proofs and establishes no equation nonexistence.
notes.text:
The supplied abstract obstruction can be checked directly. On K0={0}∪{1/r:r≥1}, f_ij has exactly one pole 1/i, value −j at the other first i isolated points, and zero at 0 and all later points. Allow every real constant shift. For fixed i, increasing j gives decreasing limit g_i with poles at the first i points. These g_i decrease to g with g(0)=0 and g(1/r)=−∞ for every r. Any two stages of one decreasing net must have a common later stage below both. A one-pole available function cannot be below two functions with distinct poles. Hence all stages of that net have one fixed pole 1/i, and equal values at 0 and every point 1/r with r>i; their limit cannot be g. This proves abstract twice-closure enlarges the family. It does not disprove closure for actual algebraic FS families.

An actual approximation warning already occurs in the granted ample domain. Let X=P1, L=O(1), p={z1=0}, and φ=log|z1| in the canonical metric. For positive rational k, f_k=max(φ,−k) is finite genuine FS on the ACTUAL O(1): append its generating system at weight −k. On the ray v_t=t ord_p, f_k=−min(t,k); all other rays have value zero. The model curve slopes −1 and then 0 give dd^c f_k=δ_(v_k)−δ_(v0). Since the trivial metric has curvature δ_(v0), M(f_k)=δ_(v_k). The raw degree-one energy is E(f_k)=½∫f_k(dδ_(v0)+dδ_(v_k))=−k/2. The f_k decrease all-point to φ, so granted ample decreasing-energy continuity gives E(φ)=−∞. Independently, the degree-m section flag has monomial weights W=−k(m−a), 0≤a≤m, whose unfloored normalized sum is −k(m+1)/(2m). Floor errors tend to zero. This is a bad approximation sequence, not nonexistence of an equation solution.

On X=Bl_p(P2), take L=2H+E. Intersections give L·E=−1 and L²=3. For 1≤j≤m, (2mH+jE)|_E=O_(P1)(−j), whose section space vanishes. The restriction sequence therefore gives H0(X,mL)=s_E^m H0(X,2mH). Thus h0(X,mL)=binomial(2m+2,2), and 2h0/m²=4+6/m+2/m² tends to 4. The correct raw big mass is vol(L)=4.

Recorded outputs: for k=1 the unfloored P1 values at m=4,8,16,32 are −5/8, −9/16, −17/32, −33/64; the limiting value is −1/2. Blowup ratios at m=1,2,4,8 are 12, 15/2, 45/8, 153/32. A finite family with 8 pole locations, 4 j-values, and 5 constant shifts has 160 members; all 4,480 candidate common-lower-member tests for pairs of distinct representative poles fail. These are exact finite diagnostics. The infinite and geometric proofs are the arguments above.

Its entire finite-energy cone is constants, energy/operator/mass are zero, and its only positive target is zero. notes.text:
Take an actual rational L with numerical class θ=0 on any retained smooth integral projective X of dimension n≥1. Constants are genuine by representing zero on the actual ample L+εA with weight-zero generators and letting ε↓0. If genuine u is generically normalized to zero, each m u is genuine in class zero and embeds as the same function into a fixed ACTUAL ample Ω. At every fixed divisorial z the granted ample bound gives −T_Ω(z)≤m u(z)≤0 for every positive integer m. Hence u(z)=0. Actual ample all-point determination makes u=0 everywhere. This proves PSH(0)=R, without fixed-degree sections of L, so nontorsion Pic0 bundles are included.

Define E_0(c)=0 and M_0(c)=0 on this whole genuine cone. These agree with genuine ample perturbations: the constant metric in the actual ample L+εA has positive raw measure ε^n(A^n)δ_(v0) and raw energy c ε^n(A^n), both tending to zero. Thus the entire E1 cone is precisely constants, reference zero, raw mass zero. Its continuous-obstacle envelope is min_Xan f; its outer energy is identically zero for both perturbation signs. A positive Radon measure of total mass zero is zero. The equation E1(0)/R→{zero measure} is a one-point bijection, and solutions are actual constants, unique modulo constants. There is no probability normalization. Domination is asserted only on the one-point normalized cone; for unnormalized different constants a zero-mass domination implication would fail. The unnormalized raw energy distance is zero on constants and is not called a separating metric.

The restriction to zero numerical class is necessary for this uniqueness statement. On X=P1×P1 let L=p1*O(1), so L is nef nonample and L²=vol(L)=0. Pull back the finite FS function max(log|z1|,−1) from the first factor. It has generic value zero and value −1 at the first-factor order-one valuation, so is nonconstant. Its actual semipositive model top measure is positive with total intersection mass L²=0, hence zero. Equivalently embed the same metric in the ACTUAL ample L+ε(p1*O(1)+p2*O(1)); the positive raw masses are 2ε(1+ε)→0, forcing the top-measure limit to zero. The constant metric has that same zero top measure. Their difference is not constant. This proves a concrete failure of zero-top-equation uniqueness on this nonzero zero-volume class, not failure of every possible lower-degree or additional-data theory.
